commercial_incentive: sells one-on-one interview prep/mock-interview sessions (plugged at end of video)
key_insights: Recommends always accepting a college interview when offered, since some schools count it toward demonstrated interest.
Distinguishes evaluative interviews (scored on a rubric, entered into the file) from informational/conversational ones meant for outreach and engagement.
At Swarthmore, evaluative interviews assessed academic insight, personal qualities, and especially intellectual curiosity, which mattered a lot at selective liberal arts colleges.
Says interviewers are typically alumni, admissions officers themselves, or trained current students, and which type interviews you usually isn't meaningful.
Safety tip: never meet an alumni interviewer at a private home; always insist on a public place or video call.

Typical questions cluster into academics, personal life outside class, and intellectual curiosity (e.g., what you've read/watched that made you think); always be ready to ask 2-3 questions that can't just be Googled.
Interview scheduling deadlines usually fall before the application deadline, so students must check the admissions site/email proactively.
Highly selective schools sometimes do invitation-only interviews (e.g., in January) for a select subset of applicants, and being invited doesn't itself signal accept or reject.
specific_numbers_or_facts: Speaker Andrew Hoffman states he was a former admissions officer/director of admissions at Swarthmore and worked at Vanderbilt.
notable_or_distinctive: Comes from someone who says he directed admissions at Swarthmore, giving concrete detail on what an actual evaluative-interview rubric covered (academic insight, personal qualities, intellectual curiosity).
reliability_notes: No garbling; claims are framed as the speaker's own admissions-office experience, but the demonstrated-interest and outcome claims (e.g., interviews 'making the difference' for waitlisted students) are anecdotal and unverifiable, and the video ends with a paid-service pitch.
